messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Stale Tests
parts:
There are a huge number of “unit” tests which really just test
regression behavior. These are particularly annoying because
there is absolutely no information about how the test content
was generated so that it can be updated when the code
necessitates it. This kind of test makes development a
pain in the ass, and at the very least any such stale file
needs to also include how it was generated.

Examples include

stan-dev/cmdstan/src/test/interface/matrix_output.csv

There are also the files in

stan-dev/stan/src/test/unit/io/test_csv_files

These are particularly frustrating as they depend on CmdStan
which introduces a circular dependency in the repositories. At
the same time, because they depend on static (usually static)
files they’ll pass even when there are inconsistencies.

Dan introduced all of these, so I think it’s fair that he provide
the code necessary to reproduce them.

Presumably they don't depend on CmdStan at test time for Stan.

I don't know what you mean by passing even when there are inconsistencies.
What's an inconsistency here?

The problem is mainly with the stan_csv_reader, which is in Stan.
The tests depend on CmdStan output isolated to constant text files
so they always pass.  This itself is fine as the tests are just testing
behavior with respect to those files.  

But then if there are any changes to, say, the samplers, then there 
is an inconsistency between what CmdStan will output and what is 
in those text files.  This will lead to CmdStan tests to then fail unless
Stan gets updated.  The tests are helping nothing in this case.
